It also adds a script for checking kit content types, a PowerShell variant, and a list of release blockers. A gets the PowerShell brace-expansion point slightly wrong, and its S1 expects a redirect to /en/ without the /agentive base path. B is long and has some padding (Lighthouse, Search Console), but most of the extra content addresses stated risks and is pasteable.

Both refuse to attest that tests passed, and both offer a checklist plus a blank sign-off template, which is the right handling. A follows the required structure with explicit Smoke, Regression, Device matrix and Content sections, pass/fail columns, and focused clarifying questions about supported devices, limit-raising policy and re-acceptance of terms. But B organizes by feature and priority, with no distinct smoke section or device matrix, so it misses the criterion. A's structure edges it ahead.
